subject.title: Telegram DM direct.tools appears accepted by config but is not reliably enforced as per-user tool policy

question: Should Telegram `channels.telegram.accounts.<account>.direct.<peer>.tools` and `toolsBySender` be treated as a hard-enforced DM security boundary, or should that accepted config surface be retired/diagnosed as unsupported?
rationale: The schema and types already advertise a security-sensitive DM policy surface, but current runtime enforcement does not read that direct config; choosing enforcement versus retirement changes operator security expectations and config compatibility.

options.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
options.body: Treat the existing direct fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with precedence, isolation, sender, account, and threaded-DM regression coverage.

options.title: Retire The Accepted Surface
options.body: Reject or migrate the direct `tools` fields and document the supported alternative so operators do not rely on a silent no-op.

options.title: Defer To Broader Policy Design
options.body: Keep this open behind the broader session/binding policy design and explicitly accept that Telegram direct policy remains unreliable until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Enforce Direct DM Policy
recommendation.body: Treat the existing direct fields as supported and implement direct-aware policy resolution with precedence, isolation, sender, account, and threaded-DM regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest shared policy and conversation-scope ownership signals for deciding the security boundary and precedence model.
